propositions: The enrich drain gate performs O(ticket-count) filesystem metadata operations (~24,000 syscalls) on every rebar write, against a declared 20ms budget, causing 486-740ms latency on stores with 4,700+ tickets.

The gate's cost is dominated by concurrent self-contention: multiple simultaneous write operations each trigger independent full-store walks that serialize on kernel vnode cache, producing a feedback loop that extends write latency by 2-6x under concurrent load.
The gate's opportunistic invocation on every write makes its budget-breach warning fire 100% of the time on large stores, rendering it a dead signal that masks genuine future breaches.

The marker-based O(1) fast path (.rebar/enrich-gate.json) proves the store quiet without re-scanning, degrading to full scan only when work is genuinely pending, achieving 35,000x latency reduction on the real store.
